quantified-tree-inventory.text: The generated inventory scans every tracked path at the bound base: one thousand two hundred and sixty-one textual files. One hundred files contain a thousand matching lines. The search includes code, speech, manifests, harnesses and history and detects both the known old adapter and the separate HTTP mock. Dispositions must be verified rather than treated as blanket deletion authority.

deletion-and-migration-responsibilities.text: Delete the old address adapter and gate, while moving shared confirmation and development adaptation duties first. Migrate test harnesses, module declarations, active docs and speech, CLI options, ownership references and the old journey pass. The dependency bump belongs with this migration. Keep historical records explicitly superseded.

why-the-http-mock-survives.text: The HTTP mock serves Koios and Blockfrost shapes for public-indexer readback controls. The attach script starts it and archive checks require it. It is independent of the old address follower and must stay. Agreement with this mock proves no real socket behavior.

why-genesis-needs-a-separate-read.text: The development runner funds ordinary wallets through transactions before printing the socket. The bare-node control separately previews the genesis wallet and expects the old index to refuse incomplete coverage. A block index cannot reconstruct an output that exists in no block, so origin coverage alone cannot justify an empty answer.

published-upstream-boundary.text: At the immutable upstream revision, library readView materializes nonempty address and asset queries with a single point from one storage transaction and preserves order and duplicates. Address-only composed views also require available asset indexing. Existing independent socket calls do not compose; the epic owner must forward the new socket release. No upstream polling is performed.
